relations.subject: Alois Anton Führer
relations.evidence: He studied Roman Catholic theology and Oriental studies at the University of Würzburg, was ordained in 1878 and received his PhD in 1879.

relations.subject: Alois Anton Führer
relations.evidence: His Sanskrit lecturer, Julius Jolly, was associated with the Bombay School of Indology.

relations.subject: Alois Anton Führer
relations.evidence: Probably due to him, he was appointed as a teacher of Sanskrit at St Xavier's Institute in Bombay.

relations.subject: Alois Anton Führer
relations.evidence: Führer came back to India in 1885 and on his arrival Alfred Comyn Lyall appointed him Curator of the Lucknow Provincial Museum.

relations.subject: Alois Anton Führer
relations.evidence: Alois Anton Führer (26 November 1853 – 5 November 1930) was a German Indologist who worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).

relations.subject: Edmund Smith
relations.evidence: Führer was replaced as Curator of the Lucknow Museum by Edmund Smith, previously the Province's Architectural Surveyor.
